Definition: to curtail, i.e. cut off the rear
BiblicalUsage: zânab means to curtail, that is cut off the rear. In Deuteronomy 25:18 we read, "How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee..." It appears again in Joshua 10:19: "And stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies, and smite the hindmost of them..."
TheologicalSignificance: zanab is to curtail, that is cut off the rear, and I believe God put it in his book for a reason, so I want to hear what it says.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
